I deliberately did not spend budget on memory_73: the competitor's entry pricing makes promotional_pricing the tempting reflex, but that memory already carries its own disconfirming detail (-12pp later-cycle retention) and self-labels as not repeatable, so matching a price war would buy conversions that decay against the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. memory_57 (referrals) is a real win but targets established customers, not the segment that is bleeding; memory_44 (enterprise sales-assist) is sound but addresses a different funnel than the one degrading. Key caveat I am carrying forward rather than resolving: every onboarding/activation memory here measures proxy outcomes (activation, completion, week-one engagement), none measures downstream qualified revenue or retention. memory_73 is the standing proof that this exact gap can hide a later-cycle reversal. Removing signup fields can also degrade lead-qualification and routing data, which would quietly hurt pipeline quality while the dashboard shows a lift.
